title: MYOPATHY WITH RIGID SPINE, SCOLIOSIS, AND MALE-LIMITED HYPERGONADOTROPIC HYPOGONADISM

intro.text: This entry describes a myopathy with rigid spine, scoliosis, and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism that affects only males (MRSG). The gene and the reports that define it could not be reliably recalled, so they are not given here.

checks.claim: Myopathy with rigid spine, scoliosis, and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism (MRSG) is a disorder that affects only males.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper is about TBCE-related disease (HRDS/KCS1 spectrum) and never mentions MRSG or a male-only disorder. In fact, its patient with a rigid spine and scoliosis (P1) is female.

paragraphs.text: Myopathy with rigid spine, scoliosis, and male-limited hypergonadotropic hypogonadism (MRSG) is a congenital or early-onset muscle disorder. It is defined by axial muscle weakness with spinal rigidity and scoliosis. Affected males also have primary (hypergonadotropic) hypogonadism. This summary is based only on the features named in the title. The specific reports, gene, and variants could not be recalled reliably and have been left out.

checks.claim: Myopathy with rigid spine, scoliosis, and male-limited hypergonadotropic hypogonadism (MRSG) is a congenital or early-onset muscle disorder.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. MRSG is not mentioned anywhere in the paper. The paper describes the TBCE c.100+1G>A homozygotes as having symptoms that start in childhood (average age 5), and it does not call this condition MRSG.

checks.claim: MRSG is defined by axial muscle weakness.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not mention or define MRSG. It describes paraspinal and proximal muscle involvement only in TBCE patients.

checks.claim: MRSG is defined by spinal rigidity.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper reports a rigid spine in TBCE c.100+1G>A homozygotes (P1 and P2), not as a defining feature of MRSG, which it never mentions.
not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper reports scoliosis in TBCE patients, not as a defining feature of MRSG, which it does not discuss.

checks.claim: Males affected by MRSG have primary (hypergonadotropic) hypogonadism.
checks.evidence_quote: We report 7 patients with a novel, milder TBCE phenotype, presenting with amyotrophy, testicular failure, and mild intellectual disability, with or without short stature.
checks.explanation: Testicular failure suggests primary hypogonadism in males. However, the abstract does not use the term hypergonadotropic and gives no gonadotropin levels.
